questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests the ability to extend behavior without modifying existing code, a hallmark of robust design.

## Key Concepts
- Decorator pattern
- Runtime composition
- Open/Closed Principle

## Code Example
```javascript
interface DataSource { read(): Buffer }
class FileSource implements DataSource { constructor(path) { this.path = path } read() { /* read file */ } }
class DataSourceDecorator implements DataSource { constructor(protected source: DataSource) {} read() { return this.source.read() } }
class EncryptDecorator extends DataSourceDecorator { read() { const data = super.read(); return encrypt(data) } }
class CompressDecorator extends DataSourceDecorator { read() { const data = super.read(); return compress(data) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test a decorator stack with different orders?
- How to handle streaming data and backpressure in decorator chains?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests choosing an architecture that stays Open-Closed, supports runtime extension of handlers, and keeps the ingestion core simple and testable.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Polymorphism
- Open-Closed Principle
- Registry-based dispatch

## Code Example
```javascript
interface FormatHandler { parse(input) }
class JsonHandler implements FormatHandler { parse(input) { /* parse JSON */ } }
class Ingestor { constructor(registry) { this.registry = registry } ingest(format, data) { return this.registry[format].parse(data) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle unknown formats at runtime?
- How would you test individual handlers and end-to-end ingestion?
